_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Equatorial Guinea covering Bubi and Fang peoples, Portuguese discovery, Spanish colonial period (Fernando Pó and Río Muni), independence 1968, Macías Nguema's reign of terror, Obiang Nguema (world's longest-ruling non-royal head of state), and oil wealth/corruption.

country_profile.capital: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

ethnic_groups.name: Fang
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant on mainland (Río Muni); Bantu people; Nguema family's ethnic group; sub-groups include Ntumu and Okak

ethnic_groups.name: Bubi
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous people of Bioko Island; pre-Fang inhabitants; distinct Bantu language and culture

ethnic_groups.name: Ndowe/Playeros
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal mainland peoples; include Combe, Benga, Bapuku, and Balengue

ethnic_groups.name: Annobonés
ethnic_groups.notes: Inhabitants of Annobón Island; Creole Portuguese speakers; mixed African-Portuguese heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Bisio/Bujeba
ethnic_groups.notes: Small mainland group near Gabonese border

ethnic_groups.name: Fernandino
ethnic_groups.notes: Creole community of Bioko; descended from freed slaves and Sierra Leonean Krio settlers; English-speaking heritage

natural_resources.notes: Oil boom since 1990s transformed economy; highest GDP per capita in Africa ($20k+) but 70% live in poverty (inequality extreme); Marathog/Zafiro/Ceiba oil fields; gas (LNG plant at Punta Europa); timber exports declining; oil production past peak and declining rapidly

military.notes: Presidential Guard (Moroccan-trained) most capable; 2004 Wonga coup attempt (Mark Thatcher/Simon Mann plot); security handled by Moroccan/Israeli advisors; militia loyal to Obiang family

infrastructure.notes: Oil wealth funded infrastructure boom (highways, new cities) but poor maintenance.

debt_aid.notes: Oil wealth means minimal foreign aid; Teodorin Obiang (VP/son) luxury spending scandals ($100M Malibu mansion, $30M Bugatti collection, seized by France/Swiss); money laundering investigations globally; economy contracting as oil declines
top_donors: Minimal; high-income status limits aid eligibility

education.notes: High nominal literacy (95%) but education quality poor; Spanish-language instruction (only Spanish-speaking African nation); French also official; scholarships to Spain/Cuba; limited domestic higher education; oil wealth not translated to education quality

diaspora_migration.notes: Spanish exile community (fled Macías regime 1970s); net emigration despite oil wealth (inequality drives departure); Cameroonians/Nigerians work in oil sector; Fang ethnic ties cross borders with Cameroon/Gabon
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Restrictive; work permits for oil sector

digital_economy.notes: Very limited digital economy; GETESA monopoly telecom; expensive/slow internet; no meaningful tech scene; oil wealth not diversified into tech; Sipopo (new capital area) has modern infrastructure but limited digital economy

country_profile.notes_unique: The only African country with Spanish as an official language; oil wealth gives it Africa's highest GDP per capita, though wealth distribution is extremely unequal.
country_profile.national_anthem: Caminemos pisando las sendas de nuestra inmensa felicidad (Let Us Tread the Paths of Our Immense Happiness)

geography.terrain: Continental: coastal plains, interior hills; Insular: volcanic islands with steep terrain
geography.notes: Only Spanish-speaking country in Africa; continental region (Río Muni) and islands (Bioko has capital; Annobón); Malabo planned to move capital to Ciudad de la Paz.

economy_extended.notes: Africa's highest GDP per capita but extreme inequality; oil revenues benefit tiny elite; oil production declining rapidly; Bata chemical explosion (2021); Ciudad de la Paz (new capital project).

health.notes: High HIV prevalence; health indicators poor despite high income level; MCDI (Medical Care Development International) operates; La Paz hospital Bata.

food_agriculture.notes: Once Africa's major cocoa exporter; oil boom devastated agriculture; 60% food imported; fish important protein source.

energy.notes: Oil production declining from peak (360kbpd 2005); LNG plant at Punta Europa; gas monetization shifting focus; Djibloho hydro dam.

transport.notes: Sipopo motorway; Malabo-Bata ferry; new roads built with oil revenue but maintenance lacking.

tourism.notes: Tourism minimal; visa restrictions; expensive destination; eco-tourism potential in rainforest.

human_rights_gender.notes: Obiang Nguema Mbasogo longest-serving non-royal head of state (since 1979); Teodorin Obiang corruption scandals; political opposition severely restricted.

security_stability.notes: Authoritarian stability; 2004 failed coup attempt (Mark Thatcher connection); tight security apparatus.

notable_historical_figures: Leoncio Evita (first African novelist in Spanish)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: State-controlled; RTVGE; no independent press; internet restricted
cultural_heritage.notes: Only African country with Spanish as primary official language; Fang people majority; both French and Portuguese also official.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Mixed: civil law (Spanish heritage) and customary law
legal_system.notes: Judiciary entirely subordinate to executive; Teodorin Obiang tried in France for ill-gotten gains; no real rule of law.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Extreme contrast between GDP per capita rank and human development indicators.

current_leader.name: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: World's longest-serving current head of state; overthrew uncle Macías Nguema; son Teodorín groomed as successor

prime_minister.name: Manuela Roka Botey
prime_minister.notes: First female PM of Equatorial Guinea

former_leaders.name: Francisco Macías Nguema
former_leaders.notes: First president; reign of terror killed ~50,000 (a third of the population); executed after Obiang's coup

910.name: Early Peoples: Bubi and Pygmy Inhabitants
910.description: Bubi people settle the island of Bioko (Fernando Pó) from the mainland; Pygmy communities inhabit the continental rainforest (Río Muni).

sub_clusters.name: Bubi Settlement of Bioko
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking Bubi people migrate to Bioko island from the Cameroon coast; develop distinct culture, yam agriculture, and chieftaincy system isolated from the mainland.

920.name: Fang Migration into Río Muni
920.description: The Fang people migrate southward into the continental territory (Río Muni); warrior culture and decentralised clan-based society.

940.name: Spanish Guinea (1843–1968)
940.description: Spain establishes effective control; British anti-slavery base at Clarence (Malabo); cocoa plantations with contract labour; Río Muni acquired; decolonisation.
